text:
maya: Quick design review — left nav density + deeplink edge cases. I sketched two approaches, want quick 👀 before tomorrow's PM sync.

maya: Problem: when we regroup items into compact groups, deep links that point to a leaf route sometimes land on the group header instead of the item. users lose context. example: /ws/alpha/models/123/overview?anchor=metrics

jorge: I hit this yesterday. The left nav highlights the parent group id instead of the child item. feels like the URL -> nav mapping only matches by prefix. :thinking_face:

priya: TL;DR: we need deterministic matching order and fallbacks. Proposed: exact match -> alias map -> prefix match. Also preserve breadcrumb trail based on the resolved item, not the nav group.

maya: Proposed URL matching pseudocode:
```
// url -> nav resolution order
if (navIndex[fullPath]) return navIndex[fullPath] // exact
if (aliasMap[fullPath]) return aliasMap[fullPath] // redirect aliases from old routes
return longestPrefixMatch(fullPath) // fallback to group
```

liam: That seems reasonable. Two nitpicks: 1) breadcrumbs must reflect resolved item label (not group id), 2) keyboard focus on deep-link should land on the highlighted item, not the top of the group.

priya: Accessibility note: ensure we set aria-current="page" on the item node and if group gets expanded for visibility, set aria-expanded="true" on the group button. Screen reader should announce the item.

maya: Copy tweak: when a deep link resolves to a group fallback, consider a subtle banner: "You were routed to the closest match — open item in this group" with a link to the intended item. small, dismissible, :info: style.

jorge: UX concern: that banner might be noisy on shared links (email -> app). maybe only show it when the resolved item != requested fullPath and user is logged in and has access. otherwise hide.

liam: also consider canonicalizing URLs in the address bar to the resolved route (replaceState) so sharing preserves the canonical link. but keep a query param like ?via=original for debugging.

priya: agree. canonicalize + add a short retention key to session for original path so we can show the banner once.

maya: Routing edge cases I listed: 1) numeric ids colliding with group slugs 2) trailing slashes + query ordering 3) old deeplinks from ops containing /# anchors. we should normalize server-side and client-side.

maya: example normalizer:
```
normalize(path) {
  path = path.replace(/\/+#.*$/, ""); // strip hash anchors
  path = path.replace(/\/+$/, ""); // drop trailing slash
  // sort query keys except `utm_*`
  return path; 
}
```

jorge: Dev question: where should aliasMap be maintained? runtime registry in console-backend or in the static nav manifest?

liam: put it in the nav manifest owned by devex. runtime should be able to patch it via feature flags. that keeps UX stable and rollout-friendly.

maya: Design ask: show both variants in the mock: (A) group-first highlight (current) vs (B) resolved item highlight + breadcrumb. I'll attach two frames in Figma after this thread.

console-bot: Deploy preview is ready: https://playground.redwood/example/nav-regression — includes longestPrefixMatch shim.

priya: Quick QA checklist: keyboard tab order, screen reader readout for expanded group, focus management on replaceState, canonical URL test, banner dismissal persists.

maya: Action items: @jorge update nav resolver PR with exact->alias->prefix order; @liam add replaceState canonicalization + ?via debug; @priya add aria-current + banner spec; maya will upload figma frames. Sync tomorrow 10:30am.

jorge: On it. small update: I'll add unit tests for ambiguous slug collisions.

liam: I'll prototype replaceState and share a short demo clip.

priya: I'll draft the a11y snippets and paste here so eng can copy.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
